editorNote: A truck line gets an end date, a terminal library gets a stable interface, and a cost-saving claim shrinks on the harder test.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027, Musk says
stories.summary: Musk said on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck output at its Texas factory around mid-2027 to free capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi. NBC reports it is unclear whether production moves elsewhere or ends.
stories.whyItMatters: A flagship product launched in 2023 now has an end date; US sales fell 48% in 2025 to 20,237, against Musk's earlier 250,000-a-year prediction.

sourceLinks.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production

stories.headline: Libghostty 1.0 ships with a stable C ABI; JetBrains terminals already run on it
stories.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto released libghostty-vt 1.0, an MIT-licensed C terminal-emulation library with semver and strict ABI promises. He lists JetBrains IDEs, KDE, and a pending Neovim switch among users.
stories.whyItMatters: A terminal engine is now a stable dependency other tools can embed, with CI on Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and WebAssembly.

stories.headline: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 15-second videos at $0.07 per second for 720p
stories.summary: Google says Omni 1.2 Flash makes and edits clips up to 15 seconds, up from 10, with multi-turn edits, and costs about 30% less than 1.1. It is generally available in the Gemini API and Google Cloud.
stories.whyItMatters: Longer clips and a roughly 30% lower price change the cost of producing short generated video through the API.

stories.headline: Hightouch: a small model that escalates to Opus matched it at 4.4x lower cost on an easy test, 1.8x on a hard one
stories.summary: Hightouch tested identity-resolution judging on 1,000 synthetic identities. A hybrid of its Jev model and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 98.8% against Opus's 99.0% on the easy set, and 95.3% against 95.1% on the hard set.
stories.whyItMatters: The '4x' headline holds for the easy set only; on the hard set the saving was about 1.8x ($2.94 vs $5.39 per 1,000), on a vendor's own benchmark.

sourceLinks.title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost

stories.headline: RealPage rent-pricing case wraps with nearly $360M to renters
stories.summary: A Tennessee federal court approved settlements from landlords totaling nearly $360 million over claims that RealPage's software helped push rents up. The companies admitted no fault and agreed to stop feeding nonpublic data into its pricing recommendations.
stories.whyItMatters: Five state attorneys general failed to block the settlements, though the judge said he would consider their concerns; claims against non-settling defendants continue.

sourceLinks.title: RealPage rent-pricing case wraps with nearly $360M to renters
